concepts.definition: Tier-1 member owning bounded work: steps, context construction and fit, acquisition, activation, evaluation, derived-surface staleness, result refinements, disposition, totality, refinement and licensing, work state and restart, cost and proportionality, and closed-result reuse. It uses, without redefining, the objects and core result algebra of FOUNDATIONS and the frame object and activate outcomes of REFERENCE_FRAME.

grounding.quote:
core for admission, activation and steps (§3); it redefines nothing those
members own. A route

concepts.label: ACTIVATION

concepts.definition: Activation of one reference frame or one declared active frame configuration on an exact subject. Its context is the activated frame's projection to the actor, never the corpus or workspace. Intake, admission, applicability and activation remain distinct even within one invocation.

grounding.quote:
A step is the activation of one reference frame, or one declared active
frame configuration, on an exact subject (REFERENCE_FRAME §1, §11). Its
context is the projection of that activated frame to the actor; the corpus
or the workspace is never the context (P0; RF-002). Intake, admission,
applicability and activation are distinct relations inside the step even
when one invocation performs all of them.

concepts.label: Step

conditions: Instance premises are selected outcome and acceptance conditions; work that may exceed one activation; actors with declared capability envelopes; and an admitted grant. Individual consequences use the premise subsets stated in the source table.
concepts.definition: Foundation-to-law family for transitions, steps and configuration, covering sections 1 and 4. These instance premises condition its governed work, are not commitments, and do not follow from finite capacity alone. The table identifies P0 as recovered; P1, P2, P3, P4a and P6 as independent; P4b as derived from P0 and P2 with the non-reacquirability premise; and P5 as derived from P0 and P6 with the open-world premise.

grounding.quote:
Foundation to law. This family, transitions, steps and configuration,
covers this section and §4. Its instance premises are: (a) a selected
outcome with its acceptance conditions; (b) work that may exceed one
activation's capacity; (c) actors with declared capability envelopes; (d)
an admitted grant. They are conditions of the work this family governs,
not commitments, and do not follow from finite capacity alone. The
standing of the consequences below is stated in
[FOUNDATIONS §3 Foundation to law](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundation-to-law).

concepts.label: Transitions, steps and configuration foundation family

concepts.definition: Material workspace state and authoritative inputs together with justifiable knowledge and explicit unknowns. Work state records workspace, governing basis, still-applicable closed results and judgments, residuals and external-effect uncertainty. An actor's context is an account of this state, not the state.

grounding.quote:
The work state of §5 records it:
the workspace, the governing basis, and the closed results and judgments
that still apply, with the residuals and the uncertainty over external
effects as the explicit unknowns. An actor's context is an account of the
current state, not the state itself
([§5](#the-workspace-and-an-actors-account)) (P3, P5).

concepts.label: Current state A

concepts.definition: Owner-defined constraint predicate comprising the selected outcome, its acceptance conditions and governing obligations. It admits multiple realised states rather than naming one state. In construction it is Z, supplied by the selected WHAT across the owning Product's Intent, Product and Specification; their descriptions refine Z.

grounding.quote:
The destination is defined by constraints: the selected outcome with its
acceptance conditions (Outcome U, [FOUNDATIONS §2](FOUNDATIONS.md#2-ontology))
and the governing obligations the work must keep. It names no single
state: its acceptance conditions admit several realised states. Its
owning authority defines it (P2, P6).

The
governing specification, the selected WHAT across the Intent, Product and
Specification of the Product that owns the work, supplies Z; its
descriptions refine Z.

concepts.label: Destination Z

concepts.definition: Bounded change from current state to next state carried out by one step. Work fitting one activation is a single transition; larger work is refined into a series, each with its own step and applicable outer obligations.

grounding.quote:
A transition is a bounded change from the current state to a next state,
carried out by one step. Where the work exceeds one activation's capacity,
the outer transformation towards the destination is refined into a series
of bounded transitions under §4 Refinement, each carried out by its own
step; work that fits one activation is a single transition. Each
transition binds the obligations it must preserve: the outer obligations
of the destination and of the governing relations it affects, as far as
they apply to it.

concepts.label: Bounded transition

concepts.definition: Corpus-owned construction relation binding A and Z, choosing work, composing steps, correcting discrepancies and claiming completion. Consumers apply this single relation; domain strategy, actor configuration, execution mechanisms and additional assurance retain their respective owners.

grounding.quote:
This subsection states the construction relation for this corpus: how a
selected construction binds its current state and destination, chooses
its work, composes its steps, corrects itself and claims completion. It
is law carried from the common construction requirement and the universal
construction model of the Product that owns this corpus, restated here at
its owner. ACTIVATION §2 to §7, EVALUATION §1, SPEC_METHOD §4 and §8,
EXECUTIVE_BASELINE, ODD and the other consumers named in the design
apply it; none restates it (P6).

concepts.label: Construction relation

concepts.definition: Three distinct subject accounts: specification is the internal reference model of required conditions; observations describe what holds; causal or predictive models explain how action may change state. These are distinct from FOUNDATIONS' accounts of a construction.

grounding.quote:
Three accounts of the subject, distinct from the accounts of a
construction ([FOUNDATIONS §2](FOUNDATIONS.md#accounts-of-a-construction)).
The specification is the internal reference model of the required
conditions. Observations describe what does hold. A causal or
predictive model explains how an action may change the state. These
accounts have different purposes and can be incomplete or wrong in
different ways; a claim about one is never taken for a claim about
another, and the applicability and adequacy of a predictive model are
claims of their own (P1).

concepts.label: Specification, observation and predictive accounts

concepts.definition: Arrangement of admissible construction and assurance serving Z within a selected resource envelope. A composition boundary is where a step's output becomes the next step's starting state; it is distinct from a categorical join, a map between categories.

grounding.quote:
A strategy arranges admissible construction and assurance to
serve Z within the selected resource envelope.

Composition boundaries. A composition boundary is the boundary between
successive steps, where one step's output becomes the next step's
starting state. It is distinct from a categorical join, which is a map
between categories ([FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#4-algebra)).

concepts.label: Strategy and composition boundaries

concepts.definition: Feedback observes, compares governing conditions, diagnoses material discrepancy, selects an authorised response, acts and observes again. Homeostasis is correction towards required conditions without a convergence or adequacy guarantee. Bugs are observed or suspected discrepancies within feature/change work and its existing intake and delivery mechanism. Diagnosis distinguishes defective realisation, inadequate requirement or design, inaccurate predictive model and insufficient observation; severity describes consequence while priority orders response.

grounding.quote:
Diagnosis distinguishes four causes: a defective realisation, an
inadequate governing requirement or design, an inaccurate predictive
model, and insufficient observation.

concepts.label: Feedback, diagnosis and bug work

concepts.definition: Exact, self-reconstructing execution intake naming the governed outcome, admitted prerequisite or experiment; subject, basis and acquirable inputs; evaluation and result algebra; affected relations and invariants; accepted transformation admissions; computational dispositions; construction and assessment authorities and grant; actor envelopes; invalidation and re-entry conditions; and, for a cost claim, allowance and spend measurement.

grounding.quote:
A step is activated from an intake sufficient to reconstruct its governing
relations without conversation history, commentary or a prior actor's memory
(P0, actor-change premise). The intake names:

concepts.label: Intake

concepts.definition: Smallest coherent causal dependency cone capable of delivering working behaviour while preserving every affected governing relation. It need not match a function, file, module, ticket field or design document. This cone is the context procedure's seed set Z, distinct in use from construction's destination predicate Z; context is its projection.

grounding.quote:
The execution unit is the smallest coherent causal dependency cone capable
of delivering working behaviour while preserving every affected governing
relation. It need not coincide with one function, file, module, ticket
field or design document (P0, P4b; provenance rc.2 SPEC_METHOD
#bounded-causal-construction). A seam whose far side can causally affect,
or be affected by, the action is inside the cone unless the basis
establishes that it cannot participate. Unrelated incompleteness outside
the cone is recorded as repricing input and does not block the bounded
claim. The cone is the seed set Z of §2; the context is its projection.

concepts.label: Execution unit

concepts.definition: Step contract with at least drafted, admitted, rejected and superseded states. Drafting and admitting are separate relations even in one invocation; that distinction implies no separate turn, carrier or ceremony. An admitted contract names one durable result and evidence surface.

grounding.quote:
Drafting a step's contract and admitting it are distinct relations, even
inside one invocation that drafts, validates, admits and executes; no
separate turn, carrier or approval ceremony is implied by the distinction.
A contract carries at minimum the states drafted, admitted, rejected and
superseded ([TICKETS §5](TICKETS.md#execution-contract-admission)).

concepts.label: Execution contract and admission

concepts.definition: Basis-bound evaluation of the predicate that a frame obligation applies to the exact subject, owned by the evaluation and scope declarations. Exclusion is the obligation's state following falsified applicability, not a result of that obligation.

grounding.quote:
The owning evaluation and scope declarations determine which frame
obligations apply to the exact subject. Their declared predicates are
evaluated from sufficient basis-bound facts: a true predicate requires the
applicable evaluation and its result; a false predicate excludes only that
obligation, under its cited authority; a missing or ambiguous premise
leaves applicability unresolved, not false.

concepts.label: Applicability and exclusion

concepts.definition: Candidate plus step-produced facts: judgments and evidence, residuals, observations, authority decisions, provenance and one construction-availability stop state. The actor's internal path is neither output nor governed.

grounding.quote:
The step's output is a candidate plus its step-produced facts: judgments with
their evidence, residuals, observations, authority decisions, provenance, and
one stop state, a value of construction availability (§3). The actor's
internal path is not part of the output
and is not governed (FOUNDATIONS §2, work boundary; provenance
[Probabilistic Work Boundary](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#probabilistic-work-boundary)).

concepts.label: Step output

concepts.definition: Allocation of task responsibilities and information exchanges to frames across the task's work; activation binds actors to frames. The active frame configuration is the portion used for one evaluation or decision. Reconfiguration is any change of allocation during work, including actors redistributing work.

grounding.quote:
A configuration allocates a task's responsibilities and information
exchanges to frames; activation binds an actor to each frame (§2). It
spans the task's work. The active frame configuration of
[FOUNDATIONS §2](FOUNDATIONS.md#frame-objects) is the part of it used for
one evaluation or decision (P0, P6).

concepts.label: Configuration and reconfiguration

conditions: The executive baseline profile is selected.
concepts.definition: Illustrative, nondefault configuration separating bounded change from delivery across tasks: Worker, specialised as Writer for documents and records, constructs; Reviewer assesses; Executive keeps the longer-term outcome, selects work and disposes within its grant while mutating nothing. The profile owns its frames, grants, limits, prohibitions and explanation.

grounding.quote:
Worker frame, specialised as Writer for documents and records, constructs;
a Reviewer frame assesses; an Executive frame keeps the longer-term
outcome, selects the next work and disposes within its decision grant, and
mutates nothing. That profile owns its frames, their grants, limits and
prohibitions, and its explanation; they apply where it is selected. It is
not the method's default. A configuration with other frames, names or
topology is evaluated as Evaluation of a configuration above states.

concepts.label: Executive configuration example

concepts.definition: Roles are configuration-allocated relations over steps, not actor kinds or a fixed inventory. Where those operations exist, constructor owns implementation and self-review, assessor independently evaluates a frozen candidate, and decision owner disposes. Other responsibilities may be allocated.

grounding.quote:
Roles are relations over steps that a configuration allocates
(Configuration above), not kinds of actor and not a fixed inventory.
Where a configuration's operations include construction, assessment or
disposition, this member names the responsibility for each: a
constructor owns the bounded implementation and its self-review; an
assessor evaluates a frozen candidate independently; a decision owner
disposes. A configuration may allocate other responsibilities.

concepts.label: Roles and delegation

concepts.definition: Declared procedure over intake seed set Z, material dependency family R and actor envelope B: compute finite unique material closure on an exact basis; project with explicit seams; test envelope fit; acquire declared inputs by exact identity. Here seed Z comprises subject, outcome and affected relations, not the destination predicate's use of Z.

grounding.quote:
Given a seed set Z (the subject, outcome and affected relations named in the
intake), a relation family R (the dependency relations whose change can
alter the result, basis validity, evidence sufficiency or authority), and
the actor's envelope B:

concepts.label: Context construction under an envelope

concepts.definition: Acquisition is read-only observation of the frame, subject and declared inputs permitted by intake, not admission or an additional actor stage. A derived surface copies, projects or compresses owning sources, names them and owns no determination; a current a_c task constraint surface is one such surface.

grounding.quote:
Acquisition. Acquisition is the read-only observation of the material a
step needs (its frame, its subject and its declared inputs) within the
inputs its intake permits it to acquire (§1 Intake). It is not an admission and not a further
actor stage; effectful work still needs its admitted contract (§1
Admission), and acquiring material grants no role, operation or decision
([FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds), What
creates no authority). A derived surface is material derived from owning
sources by copying, projection or compression, such as a projected frame
for a task; it names its sources and owns no determination. Where a
current interpretation of the subject in `a_c` exists, the constraint
surface it yields for the task is such a derived surface, under the
conditions of
[AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §9 Constraint surfaces](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#constraint-surfaces).

concepts.label: Acquisition and derived surfaces

concepts.definition: Prompt is rendered contract over typed authority, not source law. It projects current authority references, obligations, contracts, boundaries, proof expectations and fallback conditions needed by the step.

grounding.quote:
Prompt construction. A prompt is rendered contract over typed authority;
it is not source law. Prompt text must project the current authority
references, obligations, contracts, boundaries, proof expectations and
fallback conditions the step needs.

concepts.label: Prompt construction

concepts.definition: Source-identity currentness of a derived surface for a selected basis, applicable to any method and carrier. Currentness, fidelity, question-specific sufficiency and source ownership are separate matters.

grounding.quote:
This subsection owns when a derived surface (Acquisition above) is current
and when it is stale, for any method and any carrier (P3, P5, P6):

concepts.label: Staleness of derived surfaces

concepts.definition: Five result refinements with distinct questions and mapping predicates: admission/activation—lawfully admitted and activated on exact subject and basis; construction availability—a candidate is available; disposition—candidate accepted at declared boundary; ambiguity outcome—declared ambiguity resolved on exact basis; effects—intended effect occurred.

grounding.quote:
| admission and activation | may the step begin | the step is lawfully admitted and activated on the exact subject and basis |
| construction availability | did the step yield its output | a candidate is available |
| disposition | what the decision owner does with an assessed candidate | the candidate is accepted at its declared boundary |
| ambiguity outcome | what happened to a declared ambiguity | the declared ambiguity is resolved on the exact basis |
| effects | did an intended external effect occur | the intended effect occurred |

concepts.label: Core result refinements

concepts.definition: Pre-step result domain for lawful admission and activation on exact subject and basis. Values named here are activated, admission_refused(authority), admission_refused(basis), closure_unresolved, out_of_frame and activation_refusal with its cause. REFERENCE_FRAME owns the frame activate refinement and its causes and core mappings.

grounding.quote:
A step exists only after its contract is admitted (§1, Admission) and its
frame is activated on the exact subject and basis (§2). The outcomes of
admission and of context construction are owned here; each maps for the
predicate "the step is lawfully admitted and activated on the exact
subject and basis", and its cause selects its value (P5, P6; RF-005 for
the basis causes). The outcomes of frame activation are the `activate`
refinement of [REFERENCE_FRAME §5](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#5-method-functions),
which owns their causes, their predicate and their core values. Because
this predicate requires activation, a refused activation decides it with
the value REFERENCE_FRAME §5 gives; the table names those outcomes and
maps none of them again:

concepts.label: Admission and activation outcomes

conditions: Lawful activation has occurred.
concepts.definition: Result domain deciding whether the step's output exists. Output remains a candidate until evaluated: the constructed subject for a constructing step or closed results for an assessing step. Values are candidate_ready, refused, incomplete, re_entry_requested(authority) and re_entry_requested(basis).

grounding.quote:
A step's output is a candidate until evaluated (FOUNDATIONS §3, P0): the
constructed subject of a constructing step, or the closed results of an
assessing step. Construction availability records whether that output
exists (P5, P6; provenance
[work result](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/STDO_REFERENCE_FRAME_BASELINE.md#work-result)):

concepts.label: Construction availability

conditions: An assessed candidate is presented to its decision owner.
concepts.definition: Owner's acceptance result at a declared boundary, distinct from candidate availability, assessment and an assessor's recommendation. Four semantic dispositions are accept, local_repair, re_enter and reject.

grounding.quote:
The decision owner disposes an assessed candidate with one of four
semantic dispositions (§1, Roles and delegation; P6, P5; provenance rc.2
SPEC_METHOD #proportional-disposition). An assessor may recommend one; the
recommendation is evidence for the decision owner, never a disposition
([EVALUATION §4](EVALUATION.md#4-review-results)). The disposition is the
acceptance result: it consumes the candidate's availability and assessment
results and stays separate from both (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results). Each maps
to the core for the predicate "the candidate is accepted at its declared
boundary":

concepts.label: Semantic disposition

conditions: There is a declared ambiguity.
concepts.definition: Recorded result domain for whether that ambiguity is resolved on the exact basis: resolved, carried, escalated or blocked.

grounding.quote:
A declared ambiguity is resolved, carried, escalated or blocked, and the
outcome is recorded either way (§4, which also names the hard stops;
[SPEC_METHOD §5](SPEC_METHOD.md#5-ambiguity-governance-and-lifecycle)
applies this to the method's chain of authority surfaces). Each outcome
maps to the core for the predicate "the declared ambiguity is resolved on
the exact basis" (P5, P6):

concepts.label: Ambiguity outcome

conditions: A step has an intended external effect.
concepts.definition: Evidence-based result for whether the effect's declared outcome is attained: completed, not_effected or completion_unknown. Whether the effect has ended is a separate question; uncertain completion includes completion_unknown and not_effected with unestablished end.

grounding.quote:
An effectful step's intended external effect has one of three values,
mapped for the predicate "the intended effect occurred", that is, the
declared outcome of the effect is attained. The value turns on what the
admitted evidence establishes about that outcome (P5 with the open-world
premise, P6):

concepts.label: External-effect outcome and end

concepts.definition: Total handling declares next moves for all admitted condition classes, including unknown. Hard stops are nonoptional conditions regardless of ambiguity risk appetite. Reconfiguration selects a cause-responsive change after out_of_frame, invalid_basis, repeated indeterminate or incompatible results.

grounding.quote:
Next moves after any non-satisfied result are named in advance: continue
within the current contract when supported; refine; recover; yield; re-enter
the owning relation; terminate. Each admitted condition class has a declared
next move, including an explicit unknown class. Total handling does not
claim that every external condition is recognised, that an invoked provider
terminates, or that every request can be completed. A hanging external call,
an unsatisfiable demand and a lost post-effect response are three different
cases and none is solved by adding a value to the algebra.

concepts.label: Totality, hard stops and reconfiguration

concepts.definition: Refinement decomposes an outer transformation T: A → X into steps; rewrite replaces a representation, step or composite with another claimed to retain meaning. A licensing law is a subject-owner-declared permission such as associativity, commutativity or equivalence. Exact steps preserve declared meaning; approximate steps require an adequacy relation and a composite end-to-end bound.

grounding.quote:
Preservation and licensing. A refinement step decomposes a transformation
into steps, as above. A rewrite step replaces a representation, a step or
a composite by another that is claimed to keep its meaning, for example
by partitioning, regrouping, reordering, merging or substituting parts.
Each refinement layer, the steps that refine one transformation, states
what it preserves of the layer above, the transformation it refines, and
discharges that obligation (P4a, P6). A refinement or rewrite step is
admissible only under the laws declared for its subject. Its licensing law is the declared
law that permits it, such as an associativity, commutativity or
equivalence law that the subject's owner declares for the subject.

concepts.label: Refinement, rewriting and approximation

conditions: A material transition is proposed.
concepts.definition: Each admission owner's independent derivation and validation of the complete enclosing relation from authoritative inputs, followed by one semantic commit of the complete transition on an exact basis, or none.

grounding.quote:
For a material transition, each admission owner is independently
responsible for deriving and validating the complete enclosing relation
from authoritative inputs (P4b, P6; provenance
[UP-021](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#complete-enclosing-relation-admission-stdo-up-021)).
The relation contains every participant and equality join whose identity,
validity, authority, currentness or transition can affect or be affected by
admission; each crossing seam includes its relevant far side or
authoritatively establishes that the far side cannot participate. Caller or
owner assertions of completeness, validity, prior admission or authority do
not establish truth.

concepts.label: Complete enclosing-relation admission

conditions: For every admission owner and supported boundary declared by accepted design.
concepts.definition: Standing qualification of enclosing-relation admission against the supported input, state and operating or threat model. Excluded threats alone create neither acceptance predicates nor defensive-work requirements; scope expansion returns to its owner, while supported malformed inputs, stale state and effect boundaries retain checks.

grounding.quote:
Qualification of the admission law is instantiated for every admission
owner and supported boundary declared by accepted design (P6; provenance
rc.2 SPEC_METHOD #standing-structural-qualification). Case applicability
follows the supported input, state and operating or threat model. An
excluded threat alone cannot create an acceptance predicate or require
defensive work; a proposed scope expansion returns to its owning authority.
Supported malformed inputs, stale state and effect boundaries retain their
required checks:

concepts.label: Standing structural qualification

concepts.definition: Persistent object comprising workspace, governing basis, applicable closed results and judgments with invalidators, residuals and known external-effect uncertainty. Resumption re-enters the same method on current material state, possibly with another actor; checkpointing, resumption and progress accounting are generic procedures with no prescribed carrier.

grounding.quote:
Work state is the tuple of: the current persistent workspace; the governing
basis; the applicable closed results and judgments with their invalidators;
the residuals; and the known uncertainty over external effects. It is an
object (P3); its carrier (files, an event stream, another admitted owner) is
a profile or realisation choice. Resumption, checkpointing and the
progress account of this section are generic procedures
([SPEC_METHOD §11](SPEC_METHOD.md#11-build-tenant-binding)): they require
no particular carrier (P1, P6).

concepts.label: Work state, resumption and checkpoint

concepts.definition: Semantic categories: progress is accepted material movement toward the selected outcome; prerequisite work names the obligation enabled; preservation and repeated proof are evidence rather than new progress; rejected or superseded construction is churn; discovery of hidden distance revises the forecast rather than constituting negative progress. These are not a numeric algorithm.

grounding.quote:
Progress is accepted material movement toward the selected outcome;
prerequisite work names the obligation it enables; preservation and
repeated proof are evidence, not new progress; rejected or superseded
construction is churn; discovering previously hidden distance revises the
forecast and is not negative progress. Paperwork, code volume, test count,
commit count and review count are not progress by themselves. These are
semantic categories, not a numeric progress algorithm; a consumer may
derive its own progress and churn projections from them (P2).

concepts.label: Progress, prerequisite work, evidence, churn and forecast revision

conditions: Construction is delegated to a probabilistic or agentic worker.

grounding.quote:
The
normative relation runs: accepted governing basis; bounded affected
relation set; selected computational relations; delegated execution and
decision authority; construction and self-review; independent live-surface
assessment where required; one of accept, local repair, re-enter or reject
(§3); the exact accepted checkpoint; the next already-authorised bounded
action (§5).

constraints.statement: The source's normative execution relation orders accepted basis, bounded affected relations, selected computational relations, delegated execution and decision authority, construction and self-review, independent live-surface assessment where required, disposition, exact accepted checkpoint and next already-authorised bounded action.

exceptions: SPEC_METHOD §8's delivery priority is traced by family F5 at §6; its result and tenant-binding statements apply the separately identified F3 and F10 sections.

grounding.quote:
Two of its
statements apply other sections: the step's results in the core apply
§3, which family F3 traces, and the computational relations, actors and
resource limits of the tenant's binding apply SPEC_METHOD §11, which
family F10 traces. SPEC_METHOD §8 keeps its owner.

Each consumer applies the rule and decides nothing the owning section does
not (P2, P6).

constraints.statement: Consumers apply their linked owning rule without acquiring additional decisions. SPEC_METHOD §8 applies the family to execution, outcome binding, configuration and construction while retaining its ownership. Domain choices retain the named owners: outcome authority owns destination and acceptance; TICKETS owns carriers; evaluation and scope owners own applicability; selected design owns configuration and supported boundaries; applicable law and grant own assessment and reserved acceptance; decision owner accepts completion; project policy owns ambiguity risk appetite; subject owner declares licensing laws; realisation and admitted actor own strategy; strategy owner owns decomposition, order and concurrency; Product carriers own severity and priority policies; mandate owner owns ongoing-work completion.
constraints.uncertainty: External consumer loci and their additional bindings are referenced but not supplied.

grounding.quote:
A step's intake binds the current state, the
destination and the obligations: the governed outcome names the
destination, or the prerequisite towards it, that the step serves; the
exact subject and basis identify the current state it starts from; and
the affected relation set with its governing invariants holds the
obligations it preserves (Intake below; P0, P4a).
Transitions compose only as §4 Refinement permits.

constraints.statement: Every transition binds its applicable destination obligations and affected governing relations through intake: governed outcome or prerequisite identifies the destination served; exact subject and basis identify starting state; affected relations and governing invariants identify preservation duties. Composition is permitted only under refinement. Intake and work state already carry these bindings; no additional carrier is required.

grounding.quote:
Discovery. Construction, observation and evaluation change the current
state and what is known about it. A new observation may add obligations,
which join the known work, or invalidate a claim, which is re-established
or withdrawn before anything relies on it (§7). Discovery can enlarge the
known work while knowledge improves (P5, P4b).

Open work outside attention. An obligation outside a frame's current
attention stays open. A bounded view disposes of none of the work it
excludes, and the next decision keeps its material dependencies on that
work (P4b, P6).

constraints.statement: Newly discovered obligations join known work; invalidated claims must be re-established or withdrawn before reliance. Obligations outside attention remain open and materially constrain later decisions. Discovery can enlarge known work while knowledge and progress improve; remaining-item counts alone do not judge progress.

grounding.quote:
Destination change. An authorised change may revise the destination. The
change follows its owning authority and re-enters at the owning relation
(§4). A revised destination does not establish that the previous
destination was reached, and a candidate that satisfies the revised
destination is no evidence that it satisfies the previous one (P2, P6).

Completion. Work is complete only when sufficient evidence shows that the
current state satisfies the applicable destination and its acceptance
conditions; accepting that claim is the decision owner's disposition
(§3 Disposition). An empty list of known work, a count of closed or
remaining items, or the absence of a recorded counterexample does not
establish completion

constraints.statement: Destination revision requires its owning authority and re-entry at the owning relation. Neither revision nor satisfaction of the revised destination proves the previous one reached. Completion requires sufficient evidence that current state satisfies the applicable destination and acceptance conditions; acceptance belongs to the decision owner. Empty work lists, item counts and absent recorded counterexamples are insufficient.

conditions: Work cannot continue.

grounding.quote:
Stops. Work that cannot continue ends in an explicit stop that names its
cause: a step that cannot deliver its output stops with a value of
construction availability other than `candidate_ready`, and a declared
ambiguity that halts the work or exceeds the step's authority stops it
with `blocked` or `escalated` (§3). A refused admission or activation
stops the work without creating a step (§3 Admission and activation).
The work state (§5) retains the unresolved outcome, the residuals and the
obligations still owed. A stop reaches no destination and discards none
of these (P4b, P5).

constraints.statement: An explicit stop names its cause: inability to deliver output uses non-candidate_ready availability; halting or authority-exceeding declared ambiguity uses blocked or escalated; refused admission or activation creates no step. Work state retains unresolved outcome, residuals and obligations. Stopping reaches no destination and discards none of them.

grounding.quote:
The applicable declared requirements and the declared calculi of the
tenant's binding ([SPEC_METHOD §11](SPEC_METHOD.md#11-build-tenant-binding))
govern which transformations and compositions are lawful; the calculi
select no outcome. A
lawful construction can remain incomplete or fail to reach Z, and
lawfulness establishes neither delivery nor optimality. A proof about the
outcome that rests on premises retains those premises and its scope. A
selected construction may need to discover its path while performing and
evaluating work (P2, P3, P6).

constraints.statement: Construction explicitly binds current state A with its account and destination Z. External observations come through their owning interfaces; accounts may be incomplete or stale, and workspace remains the subject. Declared requirements and tenant calculi govern lawful transformations and composition but select no outcome and prove neither delivery nor optimality. Outcome proofs retain premises and scope. The specification, observation and predictive accounts may fail differently; claims about one never establish another, and predictive applicability and adequacy require their own claims.

grounding.quote:
Measures that justify a choice state
their units, boundaries and composition rules, and keep estimates,
assumptions and observations distinguishable. Several objectives can
leave alternatives incomparable; the owning criteria decide the tradeoff.
Steel thread, phased (waterfall) delivery and iterative delivery are
possible strategies, each with its own costs, feedback delays, integration risks and rework.
The selection belongs to the realisation and to the actor exercising the
admitted work authority; its material rationale is stated in existing
design or work records, and a claim that one strategy is superior states
the objectives, comparison and assumptions it depends on. No exhaustive
optimisation, universal numerical budget, scalar cost measure or preferred
strategy is imposed by this relation or its consumers (P2, P5, P6).

constraints.statement: Material strategy choices account for context, attention, time, effort, computation, communication, other relevant resources, feedback delay, uncertainty, integration exposure and rework; planning, checking and coordination also consume resources. Justifying measures declare units, boundaries and composition and distinguish estimates, assumptions and observations. Owning criteria resolve incomparable objectives. Selection belongs to realisation and the admitted actor, with rationale in existing records; superiority claims state objectives, comparison and assumptions. Context bounds holding, attention bounds use, and frames select each task contract while Z persists across its activations.

grounding.quote:
Steps
compose through compatible preconditions, effects, results and authority,
and each boundary preserves the applicable outer obligations. Refinement
can add detail and construction can change state within the permitted
variation (§4). Decomposition, delegation, concurrent work and recursive
application retain the affected obligations; independent actions may
proceed concurrently where their dependencies, effects and authority
permit. Local success supplies end-to-end success only when the required
coverage, composition compatibility and outcome evidence hold; the
obligations a chain of steps must discharge are
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Preservation through construction](FOUNDATIONS.md#preservation-through-construction).
A categorical claim about a construction meets the demonstration of
FOUNDATIONS §4 (P4a, P1, P6).

constraints.statement: Steps compose only through compatible preconditions, effects, results and authority, preserving applicable outer obligations at every boundary. Decomposition, delegation, concurrency and recursion retain affected obligations. Independent actions may run concurrently only where dependencies, effects and authority permit. Local success establishes end-to-end success only with required coverage, compatibility and outcome evidence; categorical claims require the cited FOUNDATIONS demonstration.
constraints.uncertainty: The full external chain-preservation and categorical-demonstration obligations are not supplied.

grounding.quote:
A prediction error alone does not
decide whether the required outcome holds. A revised model does not erase
the counterexample or by itself repair the realisation. Diagnosis preserves unresolved
alternatives and routes each supported repair to the owner of its cause;
the intake label supplies no repair class and no permission. Severity
describes consequence; priority orders the response under the selected
outcome, dependencies, resources and authority. A bug list projects
existing work state and creates no separate delivery or authority
mechanism (P1, P2, P5, P6).

constraints.statement: Prediction error alone does not decide outcome satisfaction; model revision neither erases a counterexample nor itself repairs realisation. Preserve unresolved causal alternatives and route supported repairs to the cause's owner. Intake labels give no repair class or permission. Priority is ordered under outcome, dependencies, resources and authority. Bug lists project existing work state and create no separate delivery or authority mechanism.

grounding.quote:
A formal induction or
termination claim supplies its premises and argument; no universal
termination proof is required before bounded work can begin, and where
such a proof is absent the claim stays within the available evidence.
Continuing work has a supported purpose under the selected strategy,
which can include reducing uncertainty or testing a bounded hypothesis.
Discovery may enlarge the known work (Transitions above), and repeated
activity alone establishes no progress. Control handles failure,
unavailable information, uncertain effects and exhausted resources
through the continuation, repair, recovery, re-entry, yield or stop that
§3, §5 and §6 name. Resumption reacquires current reality and retains
valid progress; unknown effects are resolved sufficiently before the next
dependent action (§5). Ongoing maintenance can continue under its mandate; a
delivery claim needs its completion condition. A resource limit can end
an attempt with an unresolved outcome; it establishes neither achievement
nor impossibility (P5, P2, P6).

constraints.statement: Preservation, evidence-based progress, termination and outcome satisfaction are distinct supported claims. Formal induction or termination claims supply premises and argument, but bounded work need not await a universal termination proof. Continuing work requires supported strategic purpose, including uncertainty reduction or bounded hypothesis testing; repetition alone proves no progress. Recovery retains valid work and reconciles unknown effects before dependence. Maintenance may continue under its mandate; delivery needs its completion condition. Exhaustion and unresolved attempts prove neither achievement nor impossibility.

grounding.quote:
an unavailable proof remains
an explicit obligation where the governing conditions require that proof.
Producing a candidate, proving a property and accepting delivery remain
distinct acts ([EVALUATION §5](EVALUATION.md#5-acceptance)). Completion
requires sufficient evidence against Z, including its acceptance
conditions; exhaustion or an unresolved attempt proves neither completion
nor impossibility (P5, P6). A change to Z follows its owning authority and
the re-entry rules of Transitions (Destination change); it establishes
nothing about whether the former Z was reached, and the original
counterexample stands.

constraints.statement: Evaluation preserves failure, missing coverage and uncertainty in the core. Proof, mechanical checking, testing and observed use establish only their respective scoped claims on stated subjects and assumptions. Required but unavailable proof remains an obligation. Candidate production, property proof and delivery acceptance are distinct. Destination change leaves the original counterexample standing. The construction relation adds no independent ledger, required role sequence or runtime and establishes no general solver, fixed organisation, guaranteed convergence or categorical universality.

exceptions: Allowance and spend measurement are required where the governed question is a cost claim.
Applicable design-profile laws supply affected sets, admission relations, invariants and computational dispositions where such a profile applies.
constraints.statement: Intake must reconstruct governing relations without conversation, commentary or prior memory and name every listed component. Subject, basis and permitted inputs use identity plus hash or input commit. Evaluation algebra is core or a mapped refinement. Shared machinery names its binding. Authority includes applicable frame-set, semantic, evaluation, material operation and decision kinds; grant specifies permitted operations, mutable territory and decisions reserved to others. Implementation folklore is not a source. Applicable design-profile conservation, admission-completeness, reconstruction-sufficiency and computational-projection laws are consumed without creating a second design package.
constraints.uncertainty: The referenced design-profile laws are not supplied.

exceptions: A basis establishes that the far side of a seam cannot participate.

grounding.quote:
A seam whose far side can causally affect,
or be affected by, the action is inside the cone unless the basis
establishes that it cannot participate. Unrelated incompleteness outside
the cone is recorded as repricing input and does not block the bounded
claim.

constraints.statement: Include any seam's far side that can affect or be affected by the action unless basis-supported nonparticipation is established. Record unrelated outside incompleteness as repricing input; it does not block the bounded claim.

exceptions: An explicit human override may admit the exact contract in place of deterministic admission.

grounding.quote:
Execution begins only after deterministic admission or an
explicit human override of the exact contract. The drafting actor never
infers admission from its own draft, from the presence of a carrier
(ticket, sprint entry, work contract), from lane placement or from an
`active` label. The admitted result identifies the admission mechanism and
its authority, the exact contract identity or digest, the decision and the
evidence, including any human override; absent those coordinates the
contract stays drafted or rejected, and prose asserting admission is not
admission evidence (P6; the actor cannot self-certify its own execution
basis). Admission validates the contract against its cited outcome,
prerequisite or experiment basis; it does not admit that basis, and
drafting, admitting or retaining a contract creates or renews no authority
its owner has not admitted

constraints.statement: Execution requires deterministic admission or exact-contract human override. Admission records mechanism and authority, exact contract identity or digest, decision and evidence including override. Without these coordinates the contract remains drafted or rejected; draft, carrier, lane, active label and admission prose cannot self-certify it. Validation is against the cited outcome/prerequisite/experiment basis and does not admit that basis. Drafting, admitting or retaining creates or renews no unadmitted authority.

grounding.quote:
Only an admitted contract activates a step: no
result, child completion, tool output, model response, shared actor or
lateral handoff activates another step or authorises continuation by
itself, and a profile that routes results names its instances of this
rule. Purpose and material relation: a profile and a template each stated
this list for one configuration, so the generic rule had no owner (P6).
The admitted contract names one
durable result and evidence surface; every result, withheld closure and
residual obligation is recorded there before return, a conversation return
alone is not durable evidence, and if no such surface is authorised and
available, admission refuses (P4b). Absent or rejected admission returns
the missing work authority without execution, as `admission_refused` with
its cause

constraints.statement: Only admitted contracts activate steps; results, child completion, tool output, model response, shared actors and lateral handoff alone authorise neither another step nor continuation. Routing profiles name their instances of this rule. Before return, every result, withheld closure and residual obligation is recorded on the contract's one authorised available durable evidence surface; conversation alone is insufficient. Missing surface or absent/rejected admission refuses without execution, naming the missing authority or surface and cause. TICKETS retains tier-2 carrier selection.

exceptions: A missing or ambiguous premise requiring an undeclared frame relation yields out_of_frame rather than indeterminate.

grounding.quote:
a true
predicate is `satisfied`; a false predicate is `falsified`, the
basis-bound fact that makes it false being the counterexample; a missing
or ambiguous premise is `indeterminate`, or `out_of_frame` where the
premise needs a relation the frame does not declare, and never
`falsified`. An exclusion is the state of the excluded obligation after a
`falsified` applicability result: it is no result, the obligation's own
evaluation is not performed and maps to no core value, and the obligation
leaves the required coverage of a dependent conjunction under the cited
authority of that applicability result. An obligation whose applicability is
unresolved stays in that required coverage. A predicate that its owner
declares as a disjunction that includes non-application, such as "meets
the axiom or does not apply", may be `satisfied` because the obligation
does not apply; that `satisfied` is for the declared disjunction only and
never counts toward the predicate that the obligation holds

constraints.statement: True applicability maps to satisfied and requires evaluation and result. False maps to falsified with a basis-bound counterexample and excludes only that obligation under cited authority; the excluded evaluation is unperformed, has no result or core value and leaves dependent required coverage. Missing/ambiguous premises remain indeterminate or out_of_frame, never false, and stay in required coverage. Supported inapplicability is recorded separately from result values and waives no member-acceptance criterion. A declared disjunction including nonapplication may be satisfied by nonapplication only for that disjunction, never as satisfaction of the obligation itself. Members, profiles and projects refer to this exclusion owner rather than deciding anew.

grounding.quote:
A frame name, an available
tool or a listed family triggers no activation by itself. Where
applicability needs residual semantic judgment, that judgment and its
evidence are retained as a judgment, never represented as a computed fact
(P6, P1). A required result that is absent, stale, bound to another subject
or basis, or incapable of establishing its claim cannot satisfy a dependent
conjunction ([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results));
unresolved applicability withholds the dependent claim until
sufficient evidence or the owning decision resolves it; other applicable
constraints stay in force even if only one evaluation detects them (P4b,
P5). Qualification of an applicability rule distinguishes true, false and
unknown premises, required results that are missing or bound to the wrong
subject, and a sufficient positive result, under a finite declared fixture;
a rule that always skips or always activates cannot satisfy those distinct
expected outcomes (EVALUATION §7; rc.2 RF
#applicability-and-required-results).

constraints.statement: Frame names, tools and listed families do not activate work. Residual semantic applicability judgments retain judgment status and evidence, never computed-fact status. Absent, stale, wrong-subject/basis or incapable results cannot satisfy dependent conjunctions; unresolved applicability withholds dependent claims until sufficient evidence or owner decision. Other applicable constraints persist even if detected by only one evaluation. Finite declared qualification fixtures distinguish true, false, unknown, missing/wrong-subject results and sufficient positives; always-skip and always-activate rules cannot pass these distinctions.

grounding.quote:
Explanation. The design that selects a configuration explains its
allocation, including the material resource limits it assumes, such as
context, attention, time and spend, each declared as §6 Resource limits
states, and its assumptions about failure. The
explanation is recorded in the existing design, frame declarations and
work records; no separate configuration carrier is required. It is
proportional (§6): for a direct entry, the intake states it, its
capability envelopes carrying the resource limits and its stale,
out-of-scope and re-entry conditions the failure assumptions (P2, P6).

constraints.statement: Allocation derives from operations, dependencies, available capabilities and assurance, which constrain but do not determine topology. Selecting design explains allocation, material resource limits and failure assumptions proportionally in existing design, frame or work records; direct-entry intake supplies these through envelopes and stale/out-of-scope/re-entry conditions. Evaluate against task, dependencies, actor limits, authority and assurance, never accept or reject from labels, topology, familiar roles or coordinator presence. RF-009's distinct structures stay distinct; selecting a frame grants no authority, and each activation binds subject, algebra, capability and admitted authority.
constraints.uncertainty: RF-009's structure list and §6's resource declarations are outside the supplied source.

exceptions: An explicitly bounded proxy may admit only within its existing grant.

grounding.quote:
Admission of a configuration. A configuration is admitted by the smallest
existing authority that owns the material decision the configuration
makes. One configuration may derive from several governing owners; each
keeps its own decision, and admitting the configuration creates no new
authority over them. An explicitly bounded proxy admits a configuration
only inside its existing grant (FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds, Proxy
limit). Which authority owns which decision is a binding of the method or
profile that applies this rule;

constraints.statement: Every configuration is admitted by the smallest existing authority owning its material decision. Multiple governing owners retain their own decisions; admission creates no authority over them. Method or profile binds decision ownership, with EXECUTIVE_BASELINE §16 owning the executive binding. Position in decomposition cannot move authority.

grounding.quote:
Reconfiguration. The allocation, and every reconfiguration, preserves the
material dependencies, the outstanding obligations, the effects,
including those of uncertain completion, the admitted authority and the
required independence. A reconfiguration is any change of allocation
during the work, including actors redistributing work among themselves
and the changes §4 Reconfiguration selects after a result. An outstanding
obligation and the results that depend on it move with the work. An
effect of uncertain completion is resolved sufficiently for the next
dependent action before that action (§3 Effects, §5). Required
independence keeps its authorship and evidence conditions
([EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment)), which a fresh
context alone does not meet. An adaptive or self-organised arrangement is
exempt from none of these conditions (P4b, P5, P6).

constraints.statement: Allocation and every reallocation preserve material dependencies, outstanding obligations and dependent results, effects including uncertain completion, admitted authority and required independence. Resolve uncertain effects sufficiently before dependent action. Independence retains authorship and evidence conditions; fresh context alone does not provide it. Adaptive and self-organised configurations have no exemption.

conditions: A configuration separates bounded task execution from delivery management across tasks.

grounding.quote:
Missing
information is never assumed favourable. A task result never omits a
blocker material to delivery: a compact result keeps every residual and
stop material to delivery, and its size is no evidence that none exists
(P0, P4b, P6).

Optimality. Adequacy and optimality are separate claims. A claim that a
configuration is optimal is relative to stated objectives, constraints and
comparison scope, and rests on evidence for that comparison. Familiarity,
persistence or self-organisation is no such evidence. Different
objectives or actor models can favour different configurations (P2, P6).

constraints.statement: The delivery coordinator retains the longer-term outcome and decides from sufficient bounded closed results, not task working contexts. Missing decision information is acquired through permitted inputs or further bounded evaluation, never presumed favourable. Every delivery-material blocker, residual and stop survives compact output. Independently of whether coordination is selected, adequacy and optimality are separate: optimality requires stated objectives, constraints, comparison scope and comparative evidence; familiarity, persistence or self-organisation supplies none.

grounding.quote:
Where
independent assessment supports promotion, the assessor evaluates the
exact live subject, its authority paths, proof and installed state, not
the constructor's summary (EVALUATION §3). This preserves the
independent-review relation and prescribes no actor count: one actor may
occupy different roles across different claims when independence for the
assessed claim is preserved; no role name confers an operation

constraints.statement: Promotion-supporting independent assessment examines exact live subject, authority paths, proof and installed state, not constructor summary. One actor may fill different roles across different claims only with assessed-claim independence preserved; role names confer no operation. A governing-authority-declared proxy may accept preservation, require local repair, reject violation and advance already-authorised action only within its proxy limit. Accepted basis, cone, decision envelope and re-entry conditions remove any requirement for human ceremony at every transition, but do not weaken product/release requirements for direct human acceptance.
constraints.uncertainty: The full external proxy-limit law is not supplied.

conditions: One capable context has sufficient existing work authority, exact intake and operation grant.
exceptions: Required assessment and reserved decisions remain applicable.

grounding.quote:
When one capable context has sufficient existing work authority, exact
intake and operation grant, it may enter directly as constructor. No
coordinating activation is required solely to appoint that constructor.
The applicable configuration (Configuration above) selects
coordination when material contexts, authority, capability or required
independence need it; a role or frame name alone does not create that
need. Direct entry preserves
execution-contract admission (Admission above), the smallest lawful
carrier, the required assessment and the reserved decisions; it permits
bounded work and condition-based result recording, not self-acceptance at a
boundary owned elsewhere (P0, P6).

constraints.statement: Direct constructor entry is permitted without coordination solely for appointment. Coordination is selected when material context, authority, capability or independence requires it, not from names. Direct entry retains contract admission, smallest lawful carrier, required assessment and reserved decisions; it allows bounded work and result recording, never self-acceptance at another owner's boundary.

conditions: Applicable law requires no independent assessment and reserves no acceptance.
The constructor holds the grant.
exceptions: Applicable assessment or reserved acceptance remains required.
Discovered insufficiency withholds the dependent effect and returns the question to its owner.

grounding.quote:
Recording a result without review. Where the applicable law requires no
independent assessment and reserves no acceptance, the constructor that
holds the grant may record the satisfied bounded result, with the conditions
it found satisfied and their evidence, in the existing durable result
surface (Admission above), without adding a carrier, coordinating
appointment, review or recreated design view solely to mark completion. The
recording waives no condition that actually applies, states only
conditions that were evaluated, as an actor cannot report an evaluation it
did not perform
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), Not performed), and is
no disposition at a boundary owned elsewhere
(§3 Disposition). Where an assessment or a reserved acceptance does apply,
it stays required, and an insufficiency found during the work withholds
the dependent effect and returns the question to its owner. Carriers and
profiles refer to this paragraph and add only their own carrier binding

constraints.statement: The grant-holding constructor may record satisfied bounded conditions and their evidence in the existing durable result surface without extra carrier, appointment, review or recreated design view solely for completion marking. Record only performed evaluations, waive no applicable condition and do not represent recording as another owner's disposition. Carriers and profiles add only their own carrier binding.

grounding.quote:
One bounded operation grant may cover its declared construction, status and
checkpoint sequence. Actual role transitions are recorded in the existing
work carrier; a status change alone requires neither a new grant nor
rehashing an unchanged subject. A material change to the operation, the
subject, the territory, the authority or the validity conditions requires
the affected binding to be resolved before effect. Where the selected
configuration restricts its coordinating role from mutation, as the
executive configuration (Configuration above) restricts its Executive,
the restriction that the coordinating role mutates nothing remains
applicable; an operation grant covering the sequence does not lift it
(P6, P3).

constraints.statement: One bounded grant may cover its declared construction/status/checkpoint sequence. Record actual role transitions in the existing carrier; status alone needs neither new grant nor unchanged-subject rehash. Material operation, subject, territory, authority or validity change requires binding resolution before effect. Sequence grants do not lift a selected coordinator's mutation prohibition.

grounding.quote:
If Z, R, the required-edge semantics, the basis or the scope is not
   exact, or the closure is not finite and unique on the exact basis,
   activation returns `closure_unresolved` (§3, Admission and activation)
   and no step proceeds; it does not guess.
2. Project the closure to the selected context, recording its boundary: the
   excluded, external, unresolved, translated and invalidation-sensitive
   seams (AC-011,
   [AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §4](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-011-projection);
   provenance rc.2 AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS #ac-011-projection).
   If the projection returns a gap or refusal, activation returns
   `closure_unresolved` and no step proceeds.
   Material not in the closure stays out; adjacent material does not enter
   because it exists
   ([RF-004](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-004-irrelevance-exclusion)).

constraints.statement: Seed, relation family, required-edge semantics, basis and scope must be exact and closure finite and unique; otherwise return closure_unresolved and no step proceeds. Projection records excluded, external, unresolved, translated and invalidation-sensitive seams; gap or refusal also returns closure_unresolved. Material outside closure stays outside, regardless of adjacency or availability. The procedure does not require proving no undiscovered material relation exists.
constraints.uncertainty: AC-010 and AC-011 operation definitions are external.

conditions: Actor envelope B declares a context capacity.
exceptions: Without declared context capacity no size measurement is required; other RF-002 conditions still apply.

grounding.quote:
the size of the selected context is measured before the actor reads it,
   in the unit the capacity is declared in (bytes or tokens) and over the
   boundary that the selected execution binding states for it (§6), and is
   compared with that capacity. The measurement, the capacity and the
   outcome of the comparison are recorded before the read. A fit holds
   only for the measured boundary: context outside it is recorded as not
   measured, and no fit claim covers it. The fit claim for a measured
   boundary and the step's fit judgment are distinct: the judgment is
   established from the recorded complete active inputs, or from a
   supported upper bound that includes any host-supplied context; where
   neither exists it is `indeterminate`, unless a counterexample, such as
   a measured excess, establishes `falsified`. A correct task result keeps
   its own bounded standing and does not satisfy a missing fit judgment

constraints.statement: Before reading, measure selected context in declared bytes/tokens over the execution binding's boundary and record size, capacity and comparison. Unmeasured outside context is explicitly outside the fit claim. Overall fit judgment requires recorded complete active inputs or supported upper bound including host context; otherwise indeterminate unless a counterexample such as excess establishes falsified. Correct task results cannot supply missing fit judgment. Measurement applies to every question within this declared-capacity scope, is not a budget or universal gate, and establishes fit only; adequate attention requires actual-use evidence. Other envelope dimensions follow RF-014 and other resources §6.
constraints.uncertainty: External attention-qualification and other-resource rules are not supplied.

conditions: Selected context does not fit the actor's envelope.
exceptions: Actor/envelope owner may delegate actor selection or envelope enlargement in advance through the grant.

grounding.quote:
None of these options silently reduces the required predicate: the
   obligations the step preserves stay bound
   ([§1 Transitions](#transitions)), a narrowing of them is a destination
   change under its owning authority (§1, Destination change), and what
   the selected context leaves undecided stays an explicit unknown.
   Within its grant a step selects refinement, sequencing and compression
   itself; selecting another actor or enlarging the envelope re-enters the
   owner of the grant or envelope, who may delegate that choice in the grant
   (RF-014 vests the selection in human authority; a grant is that authority
   exercised in advance). Whether a compression preserved what the
   evaluation needs is a claim with the standing of any other (EVALUATION
   §1): the compressing step records the compression and its preservation
   argument, and the claim is assessed independently only where the
   promotion it serves needs independent assessment (EVALUATION §3).

constraints.statement: Use fitting refinement, sequencing, lawful preservation compression, another fitting actor or out_of_frame, in combination as appropriate. Silent omission is forbidden. Required predicates and obligations cannot silently shrink; narrowing is owner-authorised destination change, and undecided matters remain explicit unknowns. Steps may choose refinement/sequencing/compression within their grant; actor changes or envelope enlargement re-enter the grant/envelope owner unless delegated. Compression records its preservation argument; independent assessment applies only where the served promotion requires it.

exceptions: For another task, or a stale, missing or question-insufficient surface, acquire the deciding owner sections directly as declared inputs of the exact selected basis.

grounding.quote:
Where a derived surface whose sources
are current serves the task, the actor acquires it. For another task, or
where the derived surface is stale ([Staleness of derived surfaces](#staleness-of-derived-surfaces)),
missing or insufficient for a named unresolved question, the actor acquires the deciding owner sections
directly: the owning sections that decide the task's questions, which are
declared inputs of the selected basis. Only material in the exact selected
basis is acquired: where that basis has no derived surface for the task,
its exact owner sections are used, and a candidate source, a version-line
selector or another basis is no substitute for it

constraints.statement: Acquire declared inputs by exact identity within permitted intake. Missing materialised input neither licenses reading elsewhere nor proves absence. Use the current task-serving derived surface when available, otherwise exact deciding owners under the stated fallback. Candidate sources, mutable version selectors and other bases are no substitute. Read selected material and actual subject, following needed source and coupled-obligation references; corpus availability alone is no reason to read it. Sufficiency is question-specific, never universal for a frame/corpus. Acquisition grants no authority; effectful work still requires its admitted contract.

grounding.quote:
Activation. The actor or the assigning authority selects one frame or one
declared active frame configuration capable of the evaluation. Activation
binds each reusable frame declaration to the exact subject and basis and
loads the declared material relations and evidence sources, never an
undifferentiated workspace dump; what the actor receives is the packet of
REFERENCE_FRAME §11. When no available frame and actor pairing can lawfully
perform the evaluation, activation returns `out_of_frame` where no such
pairing declares a material relation or capability the evaluation needs,
and otherwise the `activation_refusal` whose cause holds
([REFERENCE_FRAME §5](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#5-method-functions)); both are
outcomes of §3 Admission and activation. Work does not proceed through
implied context

constraints.statement: Before dependent action, report missing bindings: no frame declaring required relations yields out_of_frame; absent or unverifiable exact basis yields admission_refused(basis) at admission or activation_refusal(basis) at activation. Actor or assigning authority selects a capable frame/configuration; activation binds exact subject/basis and declared relations/evidence, never a workspace dump or implied context. No lawful pairing yields out_of_frame for missing declared relation/capability, otherwise the applicable activation_refusal. Evaluation applies declared invariants, evidence rules and algebra, distinguishing semantic law, observation, inference and decision and recording every result-sensitive assumption.
constraints.uncertainty: The full activation-refusal cause mapping and packet definition are externally owned.

exceptions: A surface whose declared sources include every owner may support the joined question.
Historical workaround text may remain only where a current requirement, design, runtime or test still needs its constraint.

grounding.quote:
Standalone scope. A derived surface or projected frame decides standalone
only the questions that its own source members own. It refuses to close a
question owned by another member, or one that joins the law of several
owners; the evaluation of that question returns `out_of_frame`
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results)) naming the owning
members, and
the question is decided from those members at their current digests or
from a derived surface whose declared sources include every owner of it

A prompt body must not carry
historical workaround prose unless the current requirement, design,
runtime or test still needs that constraint. Construction starts from the
highest live authority surface the question needs. If the prompt needs an
upstream ambiguity resolved, it names the unresolved authority gap before
fallback context is read. The prompt projects the material that
Acquisition above selects, including the raw owning members where
Acquisition falls back to them

constraints.statement: Standalone surfaces decide only source-owned questions; another owner's or multi-owner question returns out_of_frame naming owners and requires current-digest owners or an all-owner derived surface. Prompts project required current contract material, start from the highest live authority needed and declare unresolved upstream authority gaps before reading fallback. They project exact Acquisition-selected material, including raw owners on fallback, and do not become source law.

grounding.quote:
- A derived surface names the exact identity, such as the path and
  digest, of each source it was derived from and of each source whose
  change can change its content.
- It is current for a selected basis only while every source identity it
  names equals the identity of that source in the selected basis. A change
  to any of them makes it stale.
- A stale derived surface is not used as current for any question. It
  becomes current again only by regeneration from the sources at the
  selected basis, or by an explicit re-acceptance that records the new
  source identities and the finding that its content still matches them;
  until then the actor acquires the deciding owner sections directly
  (Acquisition above).
- Matching source identities establish only that the surface was derived
  from those sources. They establish neither its fidelity to them nor its
  sufficiency for a question; a surface found insufficient for a named
  question is handled as Acquisition above states.
- The owning sections at the selected basis remain the deciding source.
  Whether a current surface is insufficient for a question, or decides
  beyond its own sources, is judged against them (Standalone scope above);
  a derived surface never decides that about itself.

constraints.statement: Name exact identities for every derivation source and every source whose change can affect content. Currentness requires every named identity to equal selected-basis identity; any change makes the surface stale and unusable as current for any question. Restore only by selected-basis regeneration or explicit re-acceptance recording new identities and content-match finding; meanwhile acquire deciding owners. Matching identities establish derivation, not fidelity or sufficiency. Owners decide question sufficiency and source-scope overreach; the surface cannot certify itself. Packaging/installation carriers refine identities and re-acceptance procedures while naming this owner; PRODUCT_DEFINITION §11 does so for released carriers.
constraints.uncertainty: Carrier-specific re-acceptance procedures are not supplied.

grounding.quote:
A step returns its results in the core algebra of
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results): each evaluation it
performed returns one core value with its predicate and domain outcome,
and an evaluation it did not perform has no result. The outcomes of
admitting and activating a step, and the step's own outcomes, answer other
questions than its evaluations do. This section owns them as five
refinements of the core. Each names the question it answers and the
predicate its mapping is for, and maps each of its values to exactly one
core value; the predicate travels with the value, so no refinement's
`satisfied` counts toward another predicate
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)).
Purpose and material relation: admission, work, decisions and effects
stand in the one core (P5, P6), so a consumer that combines them cannot
read a refused activation as a step's stop, availability as fitness or
acceptance, a carried ambiguity as resolved, or an unknown effect as none.

constraints.statement: Every performed evaluation returns one core value with predicate and domain outcome; unperformed evaluations have no result. Every refinement value maps to exactly one core value for its own named predicate, never satisfying another predicate. Profiles may refine values only with a single core mapping per value and add no core value. Refused activation is not a step stop; availability is neither fitness nor acceptance; carried ambiguity is not resolution; unknown effect is not absence.

grounding.quote:
| `activated` | the contract is admitted with its admission evidence (§1), Z, R, the required-edge semantics, the basis and the scope are exact and the material closure is finite and unique (§2, step 1), its projection returns a selected context (§2, step 2), and activation returns `activated_frame` | satisfied |
| `admission_refused(authority)` | the work authority the step needs is not admitted: no admission mechanism or explicit human override admits the exact contract, or no durable result and evidence surface is authorised and available; the outcome names the missing authority or surface and its owner | out_of_frame |
| `admission_refused(basis)` | the contract's cited outcome, prerequisite or experiment basis, or the exact subject and basis it names, cannot support it; the outcome names that basis | invalid_basis |
| `closure_unresolved` | the seed set Z, the relation family R, the required-edge semantics, the basis or the scope is not exact, or the material closure is not finite and unique on the exact basis (§2, step 1; AC-010), or the projection of the closure returns a gap or refusal (§2, step 2; AC-011); the outcome names the condition that fails and the basis coordinates that leave it open | invalid_basis |
| `out_of_frame` | no available frame and actor pairing declares a material relation or capability the evaluation needs (§2, Activation), or no fit option of §2 step 3 fits the selected context to an actor's envelope | out_of_frame |
| `activation_refusal` with its cause | a cause REFERENCE_FRAME §5 states | the core value REFERENCE_FRAME §5 maps that cause to |

constraints.statement: Cause selects the result. activated→satisfied requires evidenced contract admission, exact Z/R/edge semantics/basis/scope, finite unique closure, selected projection and activated_frame. admission_refused(authority)→out_of_frame for missing exact-contract admission or authorised available durable surface, naming missing item and owner. admission_refused(basis)→invalid_basis when cited outcome/prerequisite/experiment or exact subject/basis cannot support the contract, naming basis. closure_unresolved→invalid_basis for inexact inputs, nonfinite/nonunique closure or projection gap/refusal, naming failed condition and open basis coordinates. out_of_frame→out_of_frame for missing declared relation/capability in any available pairing or no fitting option. activation_refusal retains its external cause-specific mapping, not a remapping here.
constraints.uncertainty: REFERENCE_FRAME §5's full activation_refusal mapping is unavailable.

conditions: Admission or activation is refused.

grounding.quote:
These outcomes are not values of construction availability and are not
results of a step. A refused admission or activation creates no step, no
activation of the step's frame and no work result, the closed output of a
constructing actor to its consumer; the outcome returns to the assigning
authority or the declared result carrier, and no consumer records it as a
step's stop state.
